# Motion Studio — house rules

This folder produces motion graphics (B-roll) for NOOCAP clients' short-form videos, built as code with HyperFrames and rendered locally.

## Layout
- house/STYLE.md and house/GRAPHICS.md — the shared system (delivery format, pacing, motion moves, graphics catalogue). Read these first for every client.
- clients/<client>/STYLE.md and GRAPHICS.md — only that client's differences (colours, fonts, favourites). Read them second; they win where they disagree with house.
- clients/<client>/library/ — reusable HyperFrames templates for that client.
- clients/<client>/BRIEF.md and references/ (frames/, videos/, NOTES.md) — the raw input STYLE.md and GRAPHICS.md are built from.
- clients/_template/ — copy this for every new client.
- shared/ui/<app>/ — real app screenshots and screen recordings (GitHub, Claude, ChatGPT, YouTube…), shared by all clients. Use these whenever a script names a tool; never mock up a fake UI.
- videos/<client>/inbox/ — where the team drops new audio/video + script on this computer.
- videos/<client>/<YYYY-MM-DD-topic>/ — one folder per video: source (audio or talking-head video), script.md, words.json, plan.md, out/, qa/. These folders are local to each computer and git ignores them; only four reference builds (nicole 2026-10-02-five-repos, valeri 2026-10-02-thinking-orbs and 2026-10-12-five-github-repos, lindsay 2026-10-08-ai-humanizer) are tracked, because the client style files cite them.

## Sharing this folder (git)
This folder is a clone of the private GitHub repo noocapcollab-coder/motion-studio, shared by every editor. Everything except raw footage, audio and renders is in it.
- At the start of every session run `git pull --rebase`. If it stops because of local changes, tell the editor what it found and do not discard anything.
- When you save a correction or a new rule into a style, playbook, house, tools or CLAUDE.md file, finish by committing and pushing just those files: `git add <the files>`, `git commit -m "<client or area>: <what changed>"`, `git push`. If the push is rejected, run `git pull --rebase` and push again. Never force-push, and never add anything under `videos/` or any video, audio or image-sequence file.
- Footage, finished videos and the clients' reference videos live in Drive and Notion, not in git. Download what a video needs into `videos/<client>/<job>/` on this computer.

## Client design files (Notion = source of truth)
The team edits each client's design file in Notion. At the start of every video, fetch the client's Notion design file with the Notion MCP. If it differs from clients/<client>/STYLE.md or GRAPHICS.md, update the local files to match (Notion wins) and mention what changed. When the user corrects something for a client, write it into the Notion page too and add a Change log row.
- Lindsay: https://app.notion.com/p/3ed508e99dda81b3b633e5297e0f3a33 (under Client Portals / LINDSAY GONZALES)
- Valeri: https://app.notion.com/p/3ed508e99dda8159b454fc50ca1f9cfe (under Client Portals / VALERI - DASHBOARD)
- Nicole: no Notion page yet — clients/nicole/STYLE.md (v1.0) and clients/nicole/PLAYBOOK.md are the source of truth until one is written.

## Rules
- **Confirm the computer first.** At the start of every video, say which computer this chat is linked to and which motion-studio folder is connected, and ask the editor to confirm before editing. If it's not the one they want, they open the chat in the Claude desktop app on the right computer and choose "Link to this computer".
- Never change a locked script. Flag issues, don't edit.
- Always show plan.md as a table and wait for "approved" before building.
- Format is 9:16 vertical unless told otherwise.
- Every frame must read in about one second on a phone. Respect the safe zone in house/STYLE.md (map: house/safe-zone-9x16.png): important graphics in the white area, red zone only if needed. Run the safe-zone check before delivering.
- Anything named out loud (a tool, a site, a number) appears on screen. Use real logos, never redraw them.
- Numbers count up, never just appear.
- Anything spoken in under half a second is a step on the current graphic, not a new one.
- The hook has no cuts until the first sentence ends.
- QA every render with a fresh subagent before handing it over.
- Mode A: render one clip per moment into out/, numbered in order, with 0.5s hold at the end, plus out/EDIT-NOTES.md.
- Mode B: render one full-length track timed to words.json.
- When a script needs a graphic the library lacks, build a new template, save it to the client's library and add it to GRAPHICS.md.
- When the user corrects something, ask whether it's for this client only (client file) or for everyone (house file), then add it there so it sticks.

## Pipeline (how a video is built — works on any PC)
- Start a job by copying the `build/` of the most recent video for that client (e.g. `videos/nicole/2026-10-02-five-repos/build/`, `videos/valeri/2026-10-02-thinking-orbs/build/`). Only four reference builds ship with the repo, so when a client's latest job folder is not on this computer, start from that client's kit in `tools/` instead (`nicole-reels/build`, `lindsay-reels/template/build`, `valeri-template/build`). A build holds: `gen_head.py` + `gen_clips.py` + `gen_tail.py` (concatenate to `gen.py`, run it to write `clips/*.html`), `lib/` (gsap, house.js moves, client CSS), `assemble.py`, `cut_*.py`, `safezone-check.html`, `sheet.html`.
- Inputs: Notion page (script, Raw Footage / Assets / Edited Video Drive links) → download voice/raw from Drive → transcribe with word timestamps into `source/voice.json`.
- Render each clip: `npx --yes hyperframes@0.8.92 render . -c clips/<clip>.html -o ../out/<clip>.mp4 -w 2 --quiet` (run inside `build/`).
- Safe-zone check: serve `build/` (`python3 -m http.server 8765`), open `http://localhost:8765/safezone-check.html?clips=a.html,b.html` in the browser, read `window.__report`. Fix everything it flags.
- Assemble: `python3 assemble.py preview|final|overlay|audio <version>` → `out/final`, `out/overlay` (transparent cutout), `out/audio` (VOICE, CLONE with silences removed, ON-SCREEN cues). Write `out/EDIT-NOTES.md`.
- Real assets: capture live pages with headless Chrome (`--screenshot`, light/dark via `--blink-settings=preferredColorScheme=1/0`); GitHub file/blob pages may return an error page headless — use the repo page or another real source.
- Drive limits: the Drive connector downloads/uploads only ≤10 MB per file; bigger files the user downloads/drags manually.
- AI-generated images (Higgsfield) only for illustrative props, never for logos or UIs.

## Platform notes
- Mac (Apple Silicon): transcription `mlx_whisper <audio> --model mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo --word-timestamps True --output-format json`; overlays HEVC with alpha via `hevc_videotoolbox`; alpha verified with `avconvert`.
- Windows: use `faster-whisper` (or `whisper`) for word timestamps; overlays as ProRes 4444 (`-c:v prores_ks -profile:v 4444 -pix_fmt yuva444p10le`, .mov); skip the avconvert check and verify alpha with `ffmpeg -vf alphaextract`.
- zsh (Mac): quote `"0:a:0?"`; `set -- $var` does not split words; screenshot file names contain a special space, so use globs.

## Nicole reels (talking-head + motion graphics)
- For every Nicole video, read `clients/nicole/PLAYBOOK.md` first (rules learned from Harsh's feedback: TOP hook with Nicole from frame 0, never two TOP clips in a row, Nicole on screen ~11–13 s max, big centred visuals, real assets, no empty first frames, credit creators).
- Build with `tools/nicole-reels/` (README.md = commands): copy its `build/` into the new video folder, fill `build/job.py` + `build/clips_job.py`, then gen → render → contact-sheet QA → preview + AVATAR-ALL.mp3 → avatar → tighten → sfx → finals (normal + 1.2x, with and without SFX).
- Never use the avatar video's own audio; the voice always comes from source/voice.mp3.
- Finished example jobs (clip generators and plans) are in `tools/nicole-reels/examples/`.

## Lindsay reels (hooks + full-screen body + CTA)
- For every Lindsay short, read `tools/lindsay-reels/PLAYBOOK.md` first, then `tools/lindsay-reels/README.md` for commands. Start from `tools/lindsay-reels/template/build`; copy patterns from `tools/lindsay-reels/example-aidropshipping`.
- The finished example is `tools/lindsay-reels/example-aidropshipping/` (plan and full build).

## Hook Multiplier (hook A/B versions for Instagram trial reels)
- Tool and editor guide: `tools/hook-multiplier/README.md`. One command on every computer: `npm run hooks -- --video <final.mp4> --creator <name> --count 20` (`npm run hooks:doctor` checks the computer).
- Flow: the first run probes the video, finds the hook end and writes `videos/<creator>/hooks/.work_<creator>_<video>/hooks.json`, then stops. Fill in `angle` and `text` (max 8 words, one `*emphasis*` word, at least 10 different angles across 20) for every variant, re-run to get the table and copy checks, show the table and wait for "approved", then re-run with `--approved`.
- Hooks must stay true to what the video delivers, never promise numbers or results the body doesn't back up, and never overstate a sponsor's product. Words the spell checker doesn't know (tool names) go in `allow_words` in hooks.json.
- Footage tier (a different opening B-roll per hook): save the clips into one folder (for Lindsay, animated websites from Pinterest; the mp4 for a pin is under v1.pinimg.com, see tools/lindsay-reels/PLAYBOOK.md) and add `--tier footage --broll <folder>`. Check `broll-picks.jpg` and `preview-sheet.jpg`; prefer windows that open on the site's hero, and use `crop` in hooks.json to drop mockup borders. Show both sheets with the table before rendering.
- Use the version of the cut that gets posted (with captions). Send the contact sheet and 2–3 sample files after QA; `qa-report.md` must show no problems before hand-over.

# House graphics catalogue (all clients)

The shared catalogue. Clients pick favourites, change details, or switch items off in their own `GRAPHICS.md`.
Reference codes (v01–v08, f01–f04, t01–t04) point to `clients/lindsay/references/`, where this catalogue was first built.
Every graphic is delivered as a TOP (1080×960) or FULL (1080×1920) clip. No captions; headline typography only (see STYLE.md). Each row becomes a reusable template in `library/`.
All entries use the house "rise + focus" entry from `house/STYLE.md` unless noted.

| # | Kind of line | Graphic | Reference | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | **Introducing a tool** ("it's called MiroFish", "someone built an AI tool…") | Real app icon tile + **name decode** animation beside or under it | v05, v02 @10s, v01 @1s | Accent = the tool's brand colour. Name in sans 800. |
| G2 | **Competitor callout** ("you don't need Sora or Kling anymore") | Competitor icons, each one **crossed out in red** as it's named, swapping in place | v06 | End on the "use this instead" tool as a G11 headline ("just use *this*"). |
| G3 | **List / "5 tools you need"** | Serif-italic ordinal ("the *first*") above the real icon card, tool name in bold sans below; a 1–5 counter up front | v04 | Same position and size for every item so the list reads instantly. Intro card: "these 5 *free*…" with numbers 1–5 dropping in. |
| G4 | **Several things named in one line** ("scraping, monitoring, keywords") | Cards appear **left to right, one per word**, staggered on each spoken word | v08 | Max 4 per row; a 5th wraps to a second row. Each card: icon + label (+ number if any). |
| G5 | **A number / stat** ("30,000 stars", "444x cheaper") | Big count-up. GitHub stats → real star/fork/watcher cards. Comparisons → two bars plus an "Nx cheaper/faster" pill | v08, v03 @3–6s | Count-up lands on the spoken number. |
| G6 | **Talking about a real product or feature** | Real UI screenshot or screen recording in a window frame; zoom and highlight the exact element; cursor clicks | v01 @12–16s, v07, v02 @12s | Highlight = accent outline box + slight dim of the rest. |
| G7 | **GitHub repository or file** | Live capture of the real page (dark mode); highlight the file or line, then cut into the file | v07, v02 @0s | Capture automatically from the URL. |
| G8 | **How it works / A → B** | Real icons connected by animated dashed lines; check ✓ or ! badges on outcomes | v01 @20–21s, v03 @25–28s, v04 @21–25s | Lines draw in the direction of the flow. |
| G9 | **Code / install / command** | Dark terminal card; command types in, then an output line with a green ✓ | v01 @17–18s, v04 @13–19s | Real command text from the script or README. |
| G10 | **Money / results** | Stacked notification cards (Stripe-style) sliding in with amounts | v01 @4–5s | Only real or clearly illustrative numbers; never invent claims. |
| G11 | **Punchline / key phrase** | Headline typography: sans + serif-italic word ("I built a *system*"), over a blurred real screenshot or a plain background | v05 @0.9s, v06 @3.2s, t01, t04 | 1–4 words. Usually FULL. |
| G12 | **Showing many examples / outputs** | Real websites or images as floating cards, slight 3D tilt, drifting | v01 @2–3s, @49–52s | Use for "look at what people built". |
| G13 | **World / scale** ("launches worldwide") | World map with pins or arcs lighting up | v02 (per notes) | Keep it literal. |
| G14 | **Pricing / plans** | The real pricing page or sheet, zoomed on the relevant plan | v02 (per notes: ChatGPT ads pricing) | Capture live when public. |
| G15 | **Call to action / comment keyword** | Serif italic keyword in curly quotes (“REPO”) in the client accent, TOP clip | v03 @38–39s, t03 | Keyword from the client's KEYWORDS file. |
| G16 | **Several tools / "here's a free…" roundup** | **Fanned card stack**: real UI screenshots as tilted, overlapping rounded cards dealt in one by one | f01 | 3–5 cards, each landing on its name. |
| G17 | **GitHub stars / "look how popular"** | Real repository page on an **iMac mockup** over a soft nature photo; star count highlighted in the accent; flip or count-up to the number | f04 | FULL or TOP. |
| G18 | **Big money / big number** | **Flip counter** (black tiles) under the real app icon + name, with a emphasis word in the `positive` colour | t01 | "$1,000,000,000" rolls in from the right. |
| G19 | **One tool, many models or parts** | Real UI in an outlined rounded frame on `ink`, with **tree connector lines** branching down to real icons | f03 | Lines draw top to bottom, then icons rise and focus in. |
| G20 | **Brand-block moment** (e.g. Claude) | Full-bleed block in the tool's brand colour with its real logo and wordmark | Lindsay's videos | TOP. |

**Rule of thumb:** if a line names something, show *that exact thing*. If it names a number, count it up. If it names several things, give each one its own card on its own word.

# House style (all clients)

The shared system every client starts from. A client's `clients/<client>/STYLE.md` only lists what's **different**.
**Rule: read this file first, then the client's STYLE.md. Where they disagree, the client file wins.**

## What we deliver
We make **motion-graphic clips only**. The client's editor assembles the final video (footage, captions, cuts, sound).

| Clip type | When | Canvas | File name |
|---|---|---|---|
| **TOP** | Split-screen moments: the editor puts the speaker in the bottom part | **1080 × 960** by default (client may override the split height) | `NN-top-<slug>.mp4` |
| **FULL** | The graphic covers the whole frame | **1080 × 1920** | `NN-full-<slug>.mp4` |

- **No captions** unless the client file says otherwise. Headline typography only: the word or phrase that should hit on screen.
- 30 fps, H.264, opaque background, plus a **0.5 s hold** on the last frame for handles.
- Numbered in script order. `out/EDIT-NOTES.md` lists every clip: number, TOP/FULL, the script line, the **start timecode in the voiceover**, and the length.
- Clip timing comes from the voiceover's word timestamps (`words.json`), so each clip starts on the word it illustrates.
- **Safe zone (all clients, map: `house/safe-zone-9x16.png`).** Important graphics and text go in the white area; the red zone only if really needed.
  - FULL (1080×1920): **y 211–1464**. Above y 938: **x 55–1025**. Below y 938: **x 55–915** (right side is under the Instagram buttons).
  - TOP (1080×960, top half): **y 211–938, x 55–1025**.
  - Full-bleed backgrounds and footage may fill the red zone; titles, numbers, logos, labels and key UI may not.

## The idea
Every few words, a clean, literal, *real* visual of exactly what's being said, so the video can be followed on mute.

## Pacing
- New graphic every **~1.8 s** (range 1.7–2.4 s). Nothing holds longer than ~4 s without a step inside it.
- Inside a graphic, something changes every **0.5–1 s**: a card lands, a number ticks, a cursor clicks, a line draws.
- About 60–70 % of script lines get a graphic. Lines with nothing concrete to show stay on the speaker.

## Colour (structure; values live in the client file)
Each client defines these tokens: `dark`, `ink` (deeper dark for code), `light` backgrounds (1–3), `accent` (client brand), `positive` (money / success), `negative` (cross-outs, default `#E5484D`), `text-on-light`, `text-on-dark`.
- One background per clip.
- The covered tool's own brand colour may replace the accent for that tool's moment.

## Typography (structure; fonts live in the client file)
- A **sans** for headlines and labels (bold, tight tracking, sentence case).
- An **emphasis face** for the one word that matters (house default: a serif italic, lowercase), often mixed into the same line: "I built a *system*".
- Sizes on a 1080 px canvas: hero word 150–180 px · headline 96–120 px · label 44–56 px.
- One headline per graphic, max 3–4 words, never more than 2 lines.

## Motion (house moves)
- **Signature entry "rise + focus":** from +40 px below, blur 16 → 0 px, opacity 0 → 1, scale 0.96 → 1, 0.45 s `power3.out`. Groups stagger 0.08–0.12 s.
- **Exits:** fast (0.2 s) fade + blur, or a hard cut. Most clips end on the hold frame.
- **Name decode:** tool name resolves left to right, each letter flicking through 2–3 glyphs, over ~0.5 s.
- **Cross-out:** icon enters grey at 40 % opacity → full colour (0.25 s) → a red line draws corner to corner (0.25 s).
- **Numbers always count up.** Big money or counts may use the **flip counter** (dark tiles, rolling from the right).
- **Cursor:** real macOS cursor on a slight curve; click = 0.95 scale bounce plus a ripple.
- **Camera:** slow push-in on UIs (scale 1 → 1.06); punch-in zoom onto the relevant part of a real screen.
- **No:** spins, bouncy text, wipes, glitch transitions, emoji, shaky cam.

## Real assets rule
- Logos, app icons and interfaces are **always real**: `shared/ui/`, the tool's website, or a live capture of public pages. Never redraw a logo or fake a UI.
- App icons: rounded-square tiles, radius 22 %, soft shadow.
- Screenshots: window frame, 16–24 px radius, 1 px border, soft shadow; optional accent outline or glow.

- **Screen recordings show only the app being talked about** (e.g. only the Claude UI). Cut out every frame where another window, app or desktop appears (Discord, Mission Control, screenshot toolbars), and never swap in a different recording. Hide the recording person's own name and account details (sidebars, recent chats, personal menus); OCR-check every second before using a recording. Raw recordings go in `shared/ui/<app>/_raw-do-not-use/`, clean cuts beside them with a NOTES.md. (Added 2026-10-08, Harsh.)

## Never do
- Captions or subtitles (unless the client file asks for them).
- Fake or approximate UIs and logos.
- Hold a static frame longer than ~4 s.
- Stock footage that doesn't literally match the line.

# Lindsay — Motion graphics brief

Fill in what you can. Short answers are fine, and "not sure" is a fine answer too.
Claude turns this, plus the references, into STYLE.md and GRAPHICS.md.

## 1. The content
- What are Lindsay's videos about? (e.g. AI tools, coding, YouTube growth)
- Who watches them?
- Where do they post? (Reels / TikTok / Shorts / all)
- Is Lindsay on camera (talking head with graphics over or beside them), or is it voiceover only?

## 2. Rhythm
- How often should a new visual appear? (e.g. "every 3–5 words", "every sentence")
- Should graphics cover the whole screen, split the screen with Lindsay, or pop up over her?
- How fast and energetic? (calm and clean ↔ fast and punchy)

## 3. What gets shown
Tick what applies, and add your own:
- [ ] Real app screens when a tool is named (Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub, YouTube…)
- [ ] Real screen recordings (scrolling, typing, clicking)
- [ ] Numbers that count up
- [ ] Key words as big animated text
- [ ] Logos when a brand is named
- [ ] Lists / steps
- [ ] Charts
- [ ] Other:

## 4. Look
- Colours (Lindsay's accent is currently #E4B23C; confirm or correct):
- Fonts (or "match the references"):
- Dark background, light background, or both?
- Captions: yes / no, and in what style?

## 5. Never do
- Things Lindsay or you dislike (styles, colours, effects, cheesy transitions…):

## 6. A test script
Paste one real script (and add its voiceover to `samples/` if you have it).
It becomes the first test video.

# Nicole reels: the playbook (what we learned)

Everything here comes from real feedback on Nicole's reels (Paper Cutout, Hiring Panel, Haiku Router, Claude Motion, Animations). Read it before every Nicole job. If a rule here and a newer correction from Harsh disagree, the newer correction wins, so add it here.

## The brief Harsh gives every time
"Create an eye-catching hook people will definitely get hooked on. Show proper visuals for what she's saying, simple enough that even a small kid understands, but eye-catching. Smooth visuals with good transitions. Use GitHub assets, screenshots or real video. Remove micro-pauses. Don't make the same mistakes as last time." Sometimes he adds a source of real videos (for example prompt-motion.com).

## Workflow (do not skip steps)
1. **Get the audio.** It lands in `videos/nicole/inbox/` or a Drive folder Harsh links. Make `videos/nicole/<YYYY-MM-DD-topic>/`, copy it to `source/voice.mp3`, and transcribe with word timestamps into `source/voice.json` (`python3 ~/txs.py source/voice.mp3 source/voice.json` with faster-whisper small, or mlx_whisper on the Mac).
2. **Research first.** Look up every product, repo, price or claim she names. Note anything that's off (beta only, plan limits, "up to" pricing, the transcript mishearing a CTA word) in a "Fact check" or "Things to confirm" section.
3. **Write `plan.md` as a table** (`# | Time | Type | Line | Graphic`) and wait for **"approved"**. Below the table, cover:
   - how many versions you're making
   - Nicole's screen time
   - "carried over from last time"
   - the fact check
   - copies in `toolkit/examples/plan-*.md`
4. **Gather real assets.**
   - GitHub repo pages: take zoomed screenshots and crop the logo, tagline and stats so they read big. Never use a full-page strip.
   - Real app UIs.
   - Real videos, captured with the frame-grab method below.
5. **Build the clips** (`build/clips_job.py`), render, and QA every clip on a contact sheet (`python3 sheet.py '<glob>' t1,t2,...`). Fix, then re-render.
6. **Assemble the preview.** It has placeholder panels where Nicole goes. Tighten it, make a 1.2x copy, and send both.
7. **Send the avatar audio** (`Nicole-<slug>-AVATAR-ALL.mp3`): only the parts where she's on screen, joined back to back. Harsh trains or generates the avatar from it.
8. **When the avatar arrives:**
   - Run `avatar_check.py` to see whether it was made from AVATAR-ALL or the full voice, and set `AVATAR_SRC`/`AVATAR_BODY`.
   - Run `avatar_final.py` and `tighten.py`, then `sfx.py` for sound effects and music plus 1.2x.
   - **Never use the avatar video's own audio.** The voice always comes from `source/voice.mp3`.
9. **Deliver all four** (TIGHT, TIGHT-1.2x, TIGHT-SFX, TIGHT-SFX-1.2x) into `out/final/` and send the SFX ones. If he asks for "normal speed", send the non-1.2x version.

## Layout rules (hard rules, each one came from a correction)
- **The hook is a TOP clip** (graphic in the top half, Nicole in the bottom half) **with Nicole on screen from frame 0**. Never a full face and never a full-screen Nicole.
- **Never two TOP clips in a row.** Alternate TOP and FULL.
- **Keep Nicole's screen time low**, about 11–13 s of a 40–55 s reel. She's usually in the hook plus one TOP clip in the middle. ("We are showing Nicole on screen too much.")
- **Avatar card:** a near full-width rounded card under the graphic (x18 y978 w1044 h924, radius 28) with a 6 px black border, cropped tight on head and shoulders (`CROP` in avatar_final.py).
- **Visuals must be BIG and centred.** Nothing under 36 px on screen except creator credits, and headlines are 76–96 px. Check alignment strictly on every contact sheet. ("The visuals are too small… strictly check and fix the alignment.")
- **Fill the frame.** No big empty bottom halves. If a scene leaves 600 px empty, scale it up or add the next beat there. (The step-1 GitHub frame was rejected for tiny screenshot strips and an empty bottom.)
- **No empty first frames.** Every clip opens with content already on screen (`hook0`/`enter0`), never a blank peach screen.
- **Realistic content, no grey placeholder lines.** Write real-looking resumes, invoices, chat boxes, terminals, code and files. ("Make the visuals more realistic rather than showing lines.")
- **Real assets over mockups.** Use GitHub pages, real repo stats, real UIs and real creator videos. Logos are never redrawn.
- **Anything she names appears on screen**, and numbers count up.
- **One clear idea per scene**, kid-simple metaphors: a battery for limits, a sorting machine for routing, a 1-2-3-4 ladder for steps, a "#1" medal, an invoice with a red ✕.
- **Mascot:** use Harsh's supplied Claude mascot image (`assets/imgs/mascot.png`), never a copyrighted character. Our own drawn mascot is OK.
- **Real people:** only use a real person's photo when Harsh supplies it and asks. Keep captions generic ("Anthropic right now (probably)") and never put words in a real person's mouth.
- **Credit creators.** Any third-party video (prompt-motion.com and similar) shows "made with Claude · @handle" or a handle label. The site says the videos belong to their creators.
- **Transitions:** soft zoom-through in (`xin`) and a quick blur out (`xout`) on every clip, with swaps between headlines (`swap`). Pops and back-out eases, no hard cuts mid-sentence.

## Timing rules
- A clip's start is the first word of its sentence (raw time from voice.json). Clips end where the next one starts.
- Cue animations to word start times (`// word .52 · word 1.10` comments at the top of each clip's JS).
- **Micro-pauses:** `tighten.py` cuts every silence ≥0.15 s at −38 dB down to 0.10 s, with video and audio cut together so lip sync holds.
- **Speed:** finals at 1.2x (`setpts=PTS/1.2, atempo=1.2`) plus a normal-speed copy.
- **Sound:** `sfx.py` computes the same cut map as tighten, so effects land on the tight timeline. Write events per clip in `job.py → SFX()` and match every visible action (pop on a card, stamp on a ✕, ticks on typing, whoosh on transitions, ding on a tick). There's a 120 bpm pluck music bed, sidechain-ducked under the voice.
- **ACE-Step** (AI music) needs a GPU and Hugging Face access, which this setup doesn't have. Keep the procedural SFX and music unless Harsh provides tracks.

## Writing style for any on-screen text, captions or messages to Harsh
- No lists of three for rhythm.
- No "it's not X, it's Y".
- No staccato fragments.
- Short, plain, kid-simple.

## Getting real videos when downloads are blocked
prompt-motion.com preview files are 722x406 and 4 s long. When direct download is blocked, open the `.mp4` URL in Chrome and paste the `__grab` helper (`tools/nicole-reels/grab.js`) into the page. It draws 6 frames at a time onto a canvas grid (480x270 cells, with a 150 px gap so the mouse cursor lands in the gap). Zoom-screenshot the region [0,0,1440,690] at scale 1 for t = 0, 6, 12 … 36 (10 fps), then `python3 stitch.py <screenshot-dir> <name>` rebuilds a 30 fps mp4 in `build/assets/rec/`. Show these clips inside a player frame or tile, not full screen, because they're small.

## Files in a job folder
`source/` (voice.mp3, voice.json, avatar.mp4) · `plan.md` · `build/` (job.py, clips_job.py, scripts, assets) · `out/` (clip mp4s, `final/`, `audio/`) · `qa/` (contact sheets).

# Nicole — Style (tweaks on top of the house style)

**Status: v1.0 — signed off on the FIVE REPOS video (Oct 2026).** Reference build: `videos/nicole/2026-10-02-five-repos/build/` (copy `lib/nicole.css`, `gen_clips.py`, fonts from there).
Read `house/STYLE.md` first; this file wins where they disagree. A Notion design file for Nicole is still to be written; until then THIS file is the source of truth.

## Audience and feel
- Women running their own business (inbox, leads, bookkeeping, personal brand, AI tools). Mature, warm, editorial: **not girly**.
- Show the outcome in her viewer's life first, the real UI second.

## Delivery
- **Nicole is never rendered in the frame.** TOP clips (1080×960) leave the bottom half transparent for her (cutout); FULL clips cover the frame.
- Deliver: PREVIEW (striped "NICOLE GOES HERE" placeholder), HEVC overlay with cutout, CLONE.mp3, EDIT-NOTES.md.
- No captions (her editor adds them). Pacing/retention/safe zone: house rules (≥40 % FULL, never 2 TOP in a row).

## Colour
| Token | Hex | Use |
|---|---|---|
| peach (background) | `#F4EDE4` (radial to `#FBF5EE`, fine grain) | Every background. **No wood desk. No pink.** |
| espresso | `#2B211C` | Text |
| plum | `#5B2A4A` | Serif emphasis, tickets |
| clay | `#B86B55` | Second accent, underlines, rings |
| muted | `#8A7A6E` | Small labels |

## Type (approved — keep exactly)
- Sans: **Inter** 600, tight tracking (`5 tools just went`, `never turns on`).
- Serif: **Instrument Serif Italic** for names and key words (*viral*, *Invidious*, *the tap*).
- Script: **Mrs Saint Delafield** for handwritten words (*free*, *my favourite*, *repo*, “it's fixed!”).

## Layout rules (from feedback)
- **Centre-align every graphic on the frame's true centre (x = 540).** Anything below y 938 must stay narrow enough to end before x 915.
- **No polaroids. No paper cards. No washi tape.** Text, real logos and real pages sit directly on the peach background.
- Kept: plum/clay **"No. 1" ticket stubs** for list items; small paper **script labels** on top of busy real pages ("sources", "free models") for legibility; hand-drawn clay underlines and rings.
- **Hook = real images/video with lots of movement** (e.g. the real pages of each tool scrolling live in browser cards, dealt in one by one). Never a static hook.
- Explanations = **clean real UI** in a white card (26 px radius, hairline border, soft shadow) with a slow zoom to the exact element.
- Motion: soft "settle" (rise 50 px, blur 10 → 0, 0.7 s power3.out); slow zooms; no bouncy pops.
- CTA: "Comment" (sans) + keyword in large plum script + clay underline + 1–5 tickets.

## Don't
- Pink, wood desk, polaroids, paper cards, tape, tilted elements, left/right-shifted layouts, static hooks.

# Lindsay reels — playbook (rules learned from Harsh's feedback)

Read this before every Lindsay short. It sits on top of `CLAUDE.md`, `house/STYLE.md` and `clients/lindsay/STYLE.md`.

## The standing brief (what Harsh sends with every new audio)
"Create a good eye-catching hook, show the proper visuals as per what I'm saying in a simple manner that even a small kid could understand, smooth, good transition effects, use screenshots and GitHub assets or videos, remove micropauses, download and use assets from the GitHub website and demos, and in the hook I need a good website downloaded from Pinterest."

## Workflow
0. **Confirm the computer first.** Before any editing, check which computer this chat is linked to (its name and the connected motion-studio folder) and ask: "I'll edit on <computer name> using <folder>. Use this computer?" Wait for a yes. If no computer is linked, or the editor wants a different one, tell them to open this chat in the Claude desktop app on that computer, choose "Link to this computer" and connect its motion-studio folder (Add folder). Then check the tools are installed there (node, ffmpeg, python, npx hyperframes); if not, run NEW-PC-SETUP.md section 3 first.
1. Fetch the locked script from Notion (Lindsay script pages). Never change a word of it; if it has a problem (e.g. "four ideas" but five are listed), flag it and follow the voice.
2. Voice comes from `videos/lindsay/inbox/<name>.mp3`. Remove micropauses with `scripts/tight.py` (cuts every silence over 0.12 s at -35 dB, keeps 30 ms each side) → `voice_tight.mp3`, `words_tight.json`, `cuts.json`.
3. Word timestamps: pocketsphinx forced alignment against the script (`scripts/align_template.py`, add any odd words to the `extra` pronunciation dict, it prints OOV words) or `mlx_whisper` on Mac.
4. Write `plan.md` as a table (Seg | Type | Tight time | Voice | Visual) and wait for "approved".
5. Build (see README.md), render, contact-sheet QA every clip yourself, fix, then a fresh-subagent QA on the assembled previews, then deliver.
6. Deliver the PREVIEW (with captions) plus the face-only mp3 for the avatar. When the avatar video comes back, build FINALS.

## Structure of every Lindsay short
- Two alternative hooks (H1, H2), each a TOP clip (graphic in the top half, Lindsay in the bottom half), then FULL body clips 01..N (no face), then a TOP CTA clip with Lindsay.
- Lindsay's face appears only in the hooks and the CTA. Never use the avatar video's own audio.
- Face-only mp3 for the avatar = hook1 | 0.3 s | hook2 | 0.3 s | CTA. `assemble.py audio` writes it plus `AVATAR-map.md`; check the map matches `FACE_MAP`.
- Avatars lead the voice by ~2 frames: check by envelope cross-correlation, then `tpad=start_duration=0.08:start_mode=clone` (+ stop pad).

## Visual rules
- Real assets only: real logos, real UIs, GitHub repo cards with the real star count counting up, README demo GIF frames, real screenshots (Meta Ad Library, Google Maps reviews, Gumroad, Cal.com…). Nothing fake, nothing AI-redrawn.
- The hook uses a real animated website video from Pinterest, and it MUST match what is being said (a museum site under "businesses are paying for AI" was rejected). Pick a site from the same world as the words (e.g. a local clinic / home-services site with "Book now" for "businesses pay for AI").
- Each spoken beat gets its own visual, timed to the word: name it → show it.
- The website in the hook stays BIG (full width of the top half). Never shrink it into a small card. Keep the frame clean, one idea on screen at a time, no clutter.
- Numbers always count up. Money tags, stamps (PAID ✓), check chips, red X on things being dismissed.
- Safe zone: FULL x 55–1025, y 211–1464. TOP y 211–938. Captions sit around y 1390 on FULL clips, so nothing important goes under them.
- Never show Harsh's name or email anywhere (screenshots of logged-in pages included).
- Captions: 1–3 words per group, white with shadow; merges in `captions/captions.py` MERGE (e.g. "AI-run", "$10,000"). The script constant in `captions/scripts.py` must match the voice exactly, with hyphens where MERGE joins words.
- Fonts: avoid the italic serif for keywords people must type (the T in "HUSTLE" rendered with a ball and read as "HUSTILE"); use the upright weight.
- Cream paper background (`paper2`), cards with soft brown shadows, gold accent `#e0a526`, orange tag `#d9663f`, green `#2f9e55`.

## Sound
- Music: an ACE-Step instrumental (`source/music/ace-take1.aac`), ducked under the voice.
- SFX synced to every motion beat (`sfx.py` EV table per clip: pop, whoosh, ding, tick, coin, stamp, chime, sparkle, click, spop, wdown, thud).
- Loudness -14 LUFS, peak ≤ -1.5 dBTP.

## Gotchas
- Always re-run `assemble.py` before `captions_wd.py` and `mix.py`, otherwise the music doubles.
- Root-level videos (`rw(...)`) must run to the clip end (slot + 0.5 s) with tpad-padded sources, or you get a black flash.
- Body clips use `exit=False` so there's no empty gap between clips.
- Pinterest videos: the mp4 lives at `https://v1.pinimg.com/videos/mc/720p/<hash path>.mp4` (hash from the pin's poster `i.pinimg.com/videos/thumbnails/originals/<hash>.0000000.jpg`). Chrome can block repeated downloads; allow "automatic downloads" for pinterest.com / pinimg.com, or add v1.pinimg.com to allowed domains.

# tools/nicole-reels: the Nicole reel pipeline

Read **PLAYBOOK.md** first (the rules and lessons). This README is the commands.

## Start a new video
```bash
cd videos/nicole && mkdir -p 2026-MM-DD-topic && cd 2026-MM-DD-topic
cp -r ../../../tools/nicole-reels/build . && mkdir -p source out/final out/audio qa
cp ../inbox/<audio>.mp3 source/voice.mp3
python3 ../../../tools/nicole-reels/txs.py source/voice.mp3 source/voice.json   # or mlx_whisper on Mac
```
Print the words with times, write plan.md (copy a table from `examples/plan-*.md`), and wait for "approved".

## Build
1. Edit `build/job.py`:
   - `SLUG`
   - `START` (clip start = first word of its sentence)
   - `BODY`, `BODY_SEG`, `VERSIONS`
   - `AVATAR_IV`, which is every TOP clip's raw interval
2. Write `build/clips_job.py`. The shipped file is the full Animations job, so keep its helpers block (`AN_CSS`, `stepbar`, `ladder`, `bframe`, `comp`) and replace the `clip(...)` calls. `examples/` has three more complete jobs to borrow scenes from.
   - `clip(num, slug, "top"|"full", dur, "peach", False, css, body_html, js, media=vid2(...))`
   - TOP is 1080x960 (Nicole goes under it) and FULL is 1080x1920.
   - Helpers include `SETTLE` (settle/pop/enter0/out/hook0/swap/xin/xout), `screen`, `cbar`, `typeon`, `retype`, `vid2` and `CLAUDE_MARK`.
3. Run `bash build/gen.sh`, then `bash build/render_all.sh`.
4. QA every clip with `python3 ../../../tools/nicole-reels/sheet.py '03-*' 0.3,2.0,4.5,6.8` and look at `qa/sheet-*.png`. Fix and re-render.

## Preview → avatar audio
```bash
python3 build/assemble.py preview && python3 build/assemble.py audio && python3 build/avatar_audio.py
python3 build/tighten.py --preview main
ffmpeg -i out/final/Nicole-<SLUG>-main-PREVIEW-TIGHT.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v]setpts=PTS/1.2,fps=30[v];[0:a]atempo=1.2[a]" -map "[v]" -map "[a]" out/final/Nicole-<SLUG>-main-PREVIEW-TIGHT-1.2x.mp4
```
Send the preview and `out/audio/Nicole-<SLUG>-AVATAR-ALL.mp3`.

## Avatar → finals
```bash
cp <avatar>.mp4 source/avatar.mp4
python3 build/avatar_check.py        # tells you which audio it was made from; set AVATAR_SRC/AVATAR_BODY in job.py
python3 build/avatar_final.py main   # voice comes from the preview, NEVER from the avatar file
python3 build/tighten.py main        # micro-pauses out
python3 build/sfx.py                 # -> -TIGHT-SFX.mp4 and -TIGHT-SFX-1.2x.mp4 (events in job.py SFX())
```
Also make `-TIGHT-1.2x.mp4` with the ffmpeg line above. Deliver all four.

## Render environment
HyperFrames 0.8.92 (`npx --yes hyperframes@0.8.92 render . -c clips/X.html -o ../out/X.mp4 --quiet`). On a Linux box, point `PRODUCER_HEADLESS_SHELL_PATH` / `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` at Chromium (render_all.sh has defaults). On the Mac, the installed Chrome works.

## Assets
`assets-library/` holds real prompt-motion clips (credit table in CREDITS.md) and GitHub crops. Copy what you need into `build/assets/rec` or `build/assets/shots`. `grab.js` + `stitch.py` capture more clips when downloads are blocked (see PLAYBOOK).

# Valeri — Graphics (tweaks on top of the house catalogue)

Uses every graphic in `house/GRAPHICS.md`. Valeri-specific changes:

| # | Change |
|---|---|
| G1 | Tool intro: real logo zooms slowly, then becomes the transition into the next scene (white → black, i02). |
| G2 / G4 | Several models named: show each **real model logo**; they appear on their word, then are cleared as narration moves on (i02 Claude → Qwen). |
| G5 | Stat card on white (i02): real source card, number counts up, key words highlighted. |
| G6 | Real UI in a rounded frame (6 px `#979797` outline) on the dot grid; **slow premium zoom** to the key element; red highlight box in `accent`. When a prompt is typed (Claude etc.): realistic cursor click, then typing (i01). |
| G7 | GitHub repos: **real screen recording** of the repo, clean (no bookmarks bar), slow zoom onto the repo name (i06, i01). |
| G15 | CTA: "Comment *“KEYWORD”*" in white sans + red serif italic (o01/o02). |

| — | **Favourites:** G6, G7, G1, G5, G21, G22. |
| — | **Switched off:** none yet. |

## Approved in production (ThinkingOrbs, 2026-10-02) — reuse first
Reference build: `videos/valeri/2026-10-02-thinking-orbs/build/gen_clips.py`.

| Move | Clip there | How |
|---|---|---|
| Real footage in a still grey frame, footage zooms inside (clip-path inset) | H1 | 6 px `#979797` frame on the dot grid, footage scale 1 → 1.12 over ~5 s |
| Cross-out → swap | H1 | Label crossed out in red on "anymore"; GitHub logo + red serif-italic "*open-sourced*" with drawn underline in the same spot |
| Zoom-through, white → black | 01 | Phone demo flies into camera (scale 3.2, blur) while page fades to black; next real UI resolves from blur |
| Real states, one per word | 02 | Cropped real UI pills on black, each on its word |
| Repo reveal | 03 | Real GitHub page, slow zoom to the repo name; GitHub logo + name decode; ★ count-up to the real number (finish ≥ 0.2 s before the cut) |
| Real UI + list of real options | 04 | Phone recording left; real option names pop in on the beat |
| Minecraft moment: drop it in (G22) | 05 | Real install command types; pixel block drops (steps ease, thud, pixel dust) into a chunky pixel tile; becomes the real live product |
| Red highlight box + FREE stamp | 06, 07 | Slow zoom onto the exact line of a real page, red rounded box; red FREE stamp springs in tilted |
| Confirmations as type, not boxes | 04, 05 | "already *built*", "it *works*": bold sans + red serif italic, no box, no icon |
| CTA | 08 | "Comment" white sans over the real product blurred ~30 %; “*KEYWORD*” huge red serif italic; "GitHub link" on its word |

Rhythm that worked: 9 graphics / 33 s, 4 FULL (44 %), never 2 splits in a row, hook = one split graphic with 4 steps.

## Added in production (5 GitHub repos, 2026-10-12) — reusable
Reference build: `videos/valeri/2026-10-12-five-github-repos/build/gen_clips.py` (`repo_reveal()` and `fan()` are parametric). Templates copied to `library/fgr-*.html`.

| Move | Clip there | How |
|---|---|---|
| Repo reveal with ordinal | 01, 04, 06, 08, 10 | Grey serif-italic ordinal ("*1st*" … "*the last one*"); 2x capture of the repo header in the grey frame, zoom ends cropped exactly to title row + branch row (no half rows); one centred column below: name decodes, URL, real description, ★ real count (lands ≥ 0.2 s before the cut) |
| Five-repo panel | H1, H2, 12 | One dark panel in the grey frame holding the 5 real GitHub title rows (avatar + name + Public, 2x captures), one row per beat; rows dim to 40 % on a "but…" line |
| Prompt cross-out → terminal | 05 | Real Claude prompt box in the grey frame, red cut on "prompt"; real CLI output (`task-master list`, the repo's own tasks) types in line by line |
| Real list + red box | 03 | Real skills folder in a 3-row frame, red box on the named row; box fades out, list slides, box returns on the next row |
| Count + real grid | 07 | Big number counts up from frame 0 ("500+"), then real example images from the repo pop into a 5×2 grid on "every …" |
| Pixel build → cross-out → real list (G22) | 09 | Pixel agent built bottom-up block by block on "building … from scratch", red slash, then the real README list scrolls; GitHub logo + "*open-sourced*" with drawn underline |
| Before / after cut | 11 | Real README "Before" card, red line on "cut", card collapses; real "After" card rises; "just the *steps*" |
| CTA with "plus more" | 12 | "Comment" + huge red “*KEYWORD*” over the real page blurred at 30 % (no fade from black); real repo thumbnails + dashed empty slots on "plus N more" |

Layout rules (from client review 2026-10-12, "bad alignments, not proper UI"): everything centred on x = 540 (never a left/right inset that shifts the centre); headlines are two-tone (whole line on screen dim grey, each word lights up on its beat) so a line never sits off-centre mid-reveal; no stretched captures (use the image's natural width); crop zoomed UI on row boundaries; no drawn chips standing in for real UI; dimmed elements go solid grey, not see-through.

QA lessons: counts must land ≥ 0.2 s before the cut; all scrolling/drift stops before the 0.5 s hold; never start a clip on black; a capture smaller than its frame needs the frame background set to the page colour.

# Valeri — Style (tweaks on top of the house style)

**Source of truth: the Notion design file https://app.notion.com/p/3ed508e99dda8159b454fc50ca1f9cfe; the team edits it there. This file is a local copy; Notion wins.**

**Status: v0.2** (first video signed off 2026-10-02; see GRAPHICS.md › Approved in production). Read `house/STYLE.md` first. This file only lists Valeri's differences, and it wins where they disagree.
Sources: our videos o01–o03 (his current look: **keep this essence**), inspiration i01, i02, i05, i06 (what to borrow), m01–m02 (pixel / Minecraft accents). Details in `references/NOTES.md`.

## Delivery
- TOP clips: **1080 × 960** (his split puts Valeri in the bottom half). Safe zone: see house/STYLE.md.
- Captions: his past videos have word captions (grey rounded box, techy font), added by the editor. We deliver headline typography only. **[DECIDE]** confirm the editor keeps adding captions.
- Pacing, retention, safe zone, real-assets rule: same as house (and Lindsay): **never more than 2 TOP clips in a row, at least 40 % FULL**, hook has no cut until the first sentence ends.

## The feel (from his videos + inspiration)
- **Premium, cinematic, controlled.** Polished and high-end, never generic or busy (i05).
- **One continuous edit, not separate clips.** Graphics hand over to each other: a logo zooms into the next scene, outputs appear then get cleared as the narration moves on, white flows into black (i02).
- **Multiple visual changes in the hook** to hold retention (i01).

## Colour tokens (sampled from o01–o03)
| Token | Hex | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `light` · dot grid | `#E7E7E7` + navy dots `#23304F` | His signature background: light grey with a dotted grid (o01, o03) |
| `white` | `#F7F7F7` | Clean white scenes (i02 style), with a soft grey gradient |
| `dark` | `#0D1116` | Dark scenes, dark-mode UIs, ordinal headlines ("1st", "2nd") |
| `ink` | `#000000` | Black for the white-to-black transition and logo moments (i02) |
| `frame` | `#979797` | 6 px rounded outline around UI windows (o01) |
| `accent` · red | `#F5142C` | His accent: "FREE" stamp, serif-italic emphasis ("*A fresh skill*"), highlight boxes on UIs |
| `positive` | `#3FB950` | Checkmarks, success |
| `negative` | `#E5484D` | Cross-outs |
| text | `#111111` on light · `#FFFFFF` on dark | |

## Fonts
- Sans: **Inter Display** 700–800, tight tracking (i02 "First, the model **cuts**": light grey regular + bold white/black on the key word).
- Emphasis: **Playfair Display Italic** in `accent` red ("*A fresh skill*", “QWEN”, as in o02/o03).
- Ordinals: serif italic in grey ("*1st*", "*2nd*"), as in o01.
- Pixel accent: **Press Start 2P** / pixel lettering only inside Minecraft-style moments (see below).

## Motion (Valeri-specific)
- **Zoom: slow and premium.** Ease-in-out over 1.2–2 s, scale 1 → 1.15 max, onto the exact thing (the GitHub repo name, the key line). **No fast or generic punch-zooms.**
- **Cursor clicks:** realistic macOS cursor moves to the field, clicks (press + ripple), and the prompt types in (i01).
- **Emphasis pop-ups** for key phrases ("completely free", "$0"): a card or stamp springs in over the scene, holds, then clears.
- **Seamless transitions:** match-cut and zoom-through between scenes; white ↔ black via a logo zoom (i02). Prefer these over hard cuts in FULL sequences.
- **Results in, results out:** show the output/model, then remove or transform it as the next line starts.

## Minecraft / pixel accents (m01, m02, i06)
- Pixel-art icons in a chunky framed tile (m01), a pixel mascot (m02), pixel lettering "CLAUDE CODE" (i06).
- **Use selectively:** 1–3 moments per video where it reinforces the point (a process with steps, a "build" moment, a playful contrast). Never the whole video.
- Keep it premium: pixel icons sit on his clean grid/white background with real UIs nearby; no game HUDs, no 8-bit sound or jitter.

## Don't
- **No white pill / text box with a green-check icon** ("✓ already built", "✓ it works"). It reads as generic AI-template editing. Use his headline typography instead: bold sans + one red serif-italic word ("already *built*", "it *works*"), no box.

## Favourites
G6 real UI with slow zoom · G7 real GitHub screen recording · G1 tool intro (logo zoom transition) · G5 count-up stat card (i02) · G21 emphasis pop-up · G22 pixel tile.

# PM lessons: Briefs & scripts

Mistakes the PM made once and the rule that came out of each.

## A brand describing its review process is not an approval
When: A brand email mentions script review, approval or filming as steps still to come, before any script was sent
Do: Count a script as approved only when the brand approves a script we actually sent (Script Sent Date or a sent Script email). 'Upon our approval', 'send us the script for review' and a step-by-step guide are instructions: answer what they ask for now.
Never: Set Script Approved, move a card to 6 or draft a tool-access email when no script has been sent.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.
## Include the script link in the draft email
When: Sending a script to the brand for review
Do: Add the Google Drive or Frame.io link to the script in the email body so the brand can access it immediately.
Never: Send a script email without the link to the actual file
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Draft edit.
## A script the creator's team sends by hand is a sent script
When: Our side (the creator or their team) emails the script into the brand's thread before the PM's own Script email goes out
Do: Record it like the PM's own send: Script Sent Date and Last Our Reply from that email, Next Action 'waiting on the brand to approve', and retire the PM's waiting Script draft.
Never: Leave the deal saying 'send the script' or with an empty Script Sent Date, because follow-ups and the 'script at 5 with no email' check then work from wrong facts.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.
## No team ping for work that hasn't started
When: A brand asks to pause, or any update arrives, on a deal with no brief and no video card yet
Do: Keep the hold on the deal and keep following up with the brand, but only tell the script writer or an editor when a video card exists for that deal, meaning work was actually handed to them.
Never: Never ping Rudraksh or an editor to stop or change work on a video they were never given.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.
## Scripts at Script Approval go to the brand
When: A card reaches 5- Script Approval
Do: Share the script with the brand in the deal's existing thread (WhatsApp deals: tell Harsh). When a sponsor card reaches 5 and no deal links to it, find the brand's open deal and link the card to it instead of only alerting "script ready, no deal".
Never: Leave it unsent or send it in a new thread.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: Rulebook.
## An approval with the brand's own script is an approval
When: Brand/platform says 'Approved Idea, Script', 'validated version', or Next Step 'Draft video'
Do: Card to To Film, deal Script Approved, save their version as the final script.
Never: Send it to Rudraksh as changes or a brief update.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.
## No money for the team
When: Writing cards, briefs, team pings, the access page
Do: Keep only creative content.
Never: Mention a rate, price, fee, budget, $ or payment.
Seen 3 time(s). Source: Rulebook.
## One video card per reel
When: A deal covers 2+ reels, or a brief arrives for the next reel
Do: Make a card per reel; put the next reel's brief on its own card.
Never: Put reel 2's brief on reel 1's finished card.
Seen 3 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

# PM lessons: Deals & data

Mistakes the PM made once and the rule that came out of each.

## Inbox reader lists can arrive as one string
When: Filing an email from the reader's answer
Do: Treat summary, we_promised and delivers as lists whatever shape the reader returns
Never: Let one oddly shaped field stop an email from being filed
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.
## A brand saying 'got it, we'll review' leaves the next move with the brand
When: A brand writes again only to confirm they received or can open what we sent and will come back with feedback
Do: Record it as the brand's latest email and set the deal to waiting on the brand, with the next check-in counted from that email
Never: Set the deal to 'Waiting on us', put it on Harsh's list or draft a reply to a plain acknowledgement
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.
## Only our own inboxes speak for NOOCAP
When: Reading an email in a deal thread that is signed by someone at an outside company (an agency or the brand's team)
Do: Treat anyone writing from a company domain that is not noocapcollab or a creator's own domain as the brand's side: record it as a brand reply, move Last Brand Reply, and let their address become the brand contact.
Never: File an agency's 'script is under review' or 'waiting for the client's approval' as our own email because the signer's first name matches one of our creators or the tone sounds like ours.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.
## A brand email in the creator's inbox belongs to the deal of that brand contact
When: A brand on a live deal writes only to the creator's own inbox (no reply-all), so the email has another Gmail thread id than the deal
Do: Match the deal by the sender's address (the deal's Brand Email) and creator, record the email on that deal, set Last Brand Reply and hand it to Harsh as Waiting on us; link a locked lead to the deal of that contact before any brand-name match. When that email approves the script, act on it as an approval: deal to Script Approved with the date, card to 6- To Film, and the tool-access email in the deal's own thread.
Never: Leave the deal on 'waiting for the brand' because only the lead was updated, or link a lead to another deal because the brand names overlap (Tripo 3D vs Hyper3D / Tripo 3D)
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.
## A new deal in an old thread starts with nothing from the old deal's billing
When: Opening a deal for a brand's next campaign or a new brief that arrived in an existing thread
Do: Start it at Inbound (or the stage the new emails really show) with empty invoice fields, its own Deal Memory about the new campaign only, and the brand's newest Message-ID. Billing, invoices and payment chases stay on the old deal.
Never: Copy the old deal's stage, Invoice Sent Date, Invoice Amount, invoice number or 'waiting for payment' memory onto the new deal; a copied Invoice Sent Date starts payment chases for money nobody owes.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.
## An invite to the brand's next campaign is a new deal
When: A brand whose deal is posted, invoiced or paid invites the creator to a new campaign in the same thread, even inside an email about payment and without asking for a rate
Do: Open a deal of its own at Inbound (same thread, Needs Check), ask Harsh on WhatsApp whether the creator joins, and keep the payment news on the old deal
Never: Fold the invite into the finished deal's memory or Next Action, or treat it as a brief on the old deal
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.
## A rate ask on a finished deal is a new inquiry
When: A brand whose deal is already Posted, Invoiced or Paid writes in the same thread asking for our rate for something new (another video, an event, a session).
Do: Open a separate deal at Inbound for the new ask with the thread's IDs, and put the rate question to Harsh. Leave the finished deal's memory and stage as they were.
Never: Never fold the new ask into the finished deal or rewrite its Deal Memory, and never guess a rate.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.
## A deal opened from our own handover email still needs the brand's address
When: The creator's team writes 'please add noocapcollab to this thread' and the PM opens a deal from that email
Do: Set Brand Email to the brand person our email was written to (first To/Cc address that is not ours, the creator's or a no-reply robot), and copy the Thread CC
Never: Leave Brand Email empty because the email came from our side, so no reply or script can be addressed later
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

Mistakes the PM made once and the rule that came out of each.

Never: Write conditions like 'within 3 business days of the signed agreement and deposit' when no agreement or deposit was ever discussed, or re-ask our own last question back to the brand

## Never say we sent something we only asked for
When: Writing a follow-up or reply that refers to an earlier step (a contract, brief, script, invoice)
Do: Check the deal history for who sent it. If the brand still owes it, name it as theirs: 'any news on the contract and brief from the OiiOii team?'
Never: Never write 'the brief and contract we sent' when our email only asked for them, and never record our ask as 'us: sent contract' in Deal Memory.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.
## An email we send only answers what it was about
When: The PM sends an automatic email (tool access, follow-up, script) in a thread where another draft is waiting with a brand question for Harsh
Do: Keep the waiting question alive: the auto email only closes drafts of its own kind, and a brand question about a date, money or files still goes to Harsh on WhatsApp.
Never: Let an automatic email silently reject a 'Needs you' reply that carried the brand's question.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.
## A follow-up waits from our newest email, even one sent minutes ago
When: Deciding whether a brand has gone quiet long enough for a follow-up, especially in the same run that just sent a cut or script
Do: Count the wait from the latest email we sent in the thread (the cut or script just sent included) and only chase 3 days after it
Never: Never draft a 'have you had a chance to review' follow-up right after we delivered something, counted from an older Last Our Reply

## No follow-up to the brand while we owe the next cut
When: A cut went to the brand, they sent changes or asked for a reshoot, and the editor or creator is working on it, even if the creator's card still shows 9- Approval.
Do: Treat the EDIT TRACKER row on Changes (or a Next Action like "editor making the brand's changes" or a reshoot) as our move. Send the revised cut when it is done; if it is late, tell Harsh once.
Never: Never send the brand a check-in that only repeats our last email or promises the cut 'in the next few days'.

## A follow-up counts from the brand's newest message, in any inbox
When: A brand writes on a deal from or to the creator's own inbox (not the noocapcollab thread), e.g. 'sent it to the client for review'
Do: Record that message on the deal (Last Brand Reply, memory) and wait 3 days from it before a gentle nudge that acknowledges what they said.
Never: Send 'do you have any feedback yet?' hours after the brand told us the script is with their client.

## Count every follow-up in the thread, not just the counter
When: Deciding whether to send another follow-up on a script or video the brand hasn't answered
Do: Count the follow-ups in the deal's history since the brand last wrote (including ones sent by hand). At 5 for a script, stop and hand it to Harsh once.
Never: Draft a follow-up numbered from a stale counter, or promise to start work 'right away' to push a silent brand.

When: A draft is waiting in Approvals and the brand writes again on that deal (in any of our inboxes, including the creator's own)

Never: Leave a 'did you get it?' or 'just making sure this reached you' draft waiting after the brand has already confirmed receipt or acted on it.

## Answer the brand's newest email, to the person who wrote it
When: Replying in a thread where the brand's latest email changes the subject (hands payment to a colleague, pitches a new brand, asks a rate)
Do: Read the newest message first. Greet and address whoever wrote it, answer exactly what it asks, and send a rate or new-brand question to Harsh (it opens its own Inbound deal).
Never: Answer an older question nobody asked again, greet someone who did not write, or skip the question the brand actually asked.

When: Writing any email to a brand, including a resend from a creator's inbox
Do: Put every address in the deal's Thread CC into Cc, plus noocapcollab when the brand was asked to reply all.

When: Mentioning when a video posts
Do: Use the video card's POST DATE, and only when it is given in the facts.

Do: Let unsent first replies to brand pitches expire after 5 days; reject drafts that the thread already moved past.

Mistakes the PM made once and the rule that came out of each.

## A due date in a brand email comes from the brand's terms
When: Writing a payment chase or reminder that names a due date
Do: Quote a due date only when the thread or the deal's Payment Terms give it (Net 30 agreed, the brand's own 'paid on 13/11'). When no terms were agreed, ask when we can expect the payment instead. Match the count: two invoices sent = 'the two invoices'.
Never: Quote a due date that was filled in as a Net 30 guess, or call two invoices 'the invoice'.

## One invoice email per Stripe invoice
When: Drafting an invoice email for a Stripe invoice, from WhatsApp or from the heartbeat
Do: Before drafting, look for an Approvals row with the same Stripe invoice id that is waiting or already sent; if there is one, draft nothing.
Never: Draft a second invoice or payment-chase email for an invoice that already has one, or put two cards for one invoice in front of Harsh.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.
## Chase payment where the brand said invoices go
When: A brand names a finance or accounts address for invoices, or asks for reminders in the invoice thread
Do: Send invoices and every payment chase to that address, in the thread where the invoice went, with the usual contact on Cc.
Never: Never chase payment in the contact's deal thread once the brand named a finance address, and never put an estimated date in a brand email.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.
## Answer the brand's question before chasing money
When: A payment chase is due but the brand's latest email to us is a question we have not answered
Do: Hold the chase. Get the answer (ask Harsh on WhatsApp if only he knows) and send that first; the payment ask can ride in the same email.
Never: Draft a payment chase that skips or guesses the answer to the brand's open question.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.
## Chase where the brand told us to chase
When: Writing a payment chase or reminder on a deal where the brand said how invoices or reminders must be sent (which thread, which finance address, which portal)
Do: Read the thread for the brand's own instructions first and follow them: reply in the thread the invoice went out in and copy the finance address they named. If the deal's Thread ID points at the old collab thread, switch it to the invoice thread before drafting.
Never: Chase in the collab thread without finance when the brand asked for the invoice thread with finance in copy, or send a second chase the same day as one already sent by hand.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.
## Invoiced only when an invoice really went out
When: Reading an email that mentions an invoice, or creating a deal from an old thread
Do: Move a deal to Invoiced only when our invoice was actually sent (Approvals, Stripe, or the creator's own invoice to the brand) and record its date. When the brand sends billing details, raise the invoice; asking for details is not invoicing.
Never: Never set Invoiced or Paid from the AI's reading of an email, and never leave a deal at Invoiced with no invoice date, number or Stripe invoice.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.
## Stop chasing billing details after 3 reminders or when the brand pays through a platform
When: The video is posted and the invoice needs the brand's company details
Do: Count Billing Reminders Sent. At 3, stop and tell Harsh once. If the brand pays through Gusto, Faved, creator.co or a similar portal, use that portal and don't ask for invoice details. Never nudge while our own latest email in the thread is still unanswered.
Never: Draft a 4th billing reminder, or a reminder hours after our last email.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.
## A claimed payment needs proof
When: A brand says 'we've already paid' with nothing attached
Do: Check Stripe, then earlier proof in the deal; if neither, ask for the transfer receipt or reference.
Never: Mark it paid, or ask again for proof they already sent earlier in the thread.
Seen 4 time(s). Source: Rulebook.
## Upfront money does not close the deal
When: A payment arrives before the video is posted
Do: Record it as an upfront part payment and keep the deal open.
Never: Mark the whole deal Paid.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.
## Brand asked for the invoice = raise it
When: A brand asks for the invoice
Do: Draft the invoice right away (Brad is invoiced by hand, never flag his Stripe).
Never: Reply that it will come later.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.
## Retire a before-due reminder after the due date
When: A payment chase is waiting and the due date passes
Do: Replace it with a real past-due chase.
Never: Send 'is it on track for the due date' after the date.

When: A brand writes about paying

Never: Mark Paid from a promise, ask for proof of a payment that hasn't happened, or send an 'is it on track' check-in before the date the brand already gave.

When: Writing an invoice email
Do: One sentence and the payment details.

# PM lessons: Video & editors

Mistakes the PM made once and the rule that came out of each.

## A cut link after script approval is a Draft video email
When: Someone on WhatsApp or chat hands over an edited video link (Drive, Frame.io) to send to a brand whose script is already approved
Do: File it as Kind 'Draft video' so the deal moves to Submitted and the board card moves to 9- Approval Brand/Creator, and write one sentence that hands over the cut
Never: File a cut as a Script email or ask for 'feedback on the script' once the script is approved
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.
## A revised cut email only hands over the cut
When: Sending a cut to a brand, above all a revised cut after their changes
Do: Say in one sentence that the link is the revised cut with the changes they asked for, and nothing else. A billing or other question the brand asked in the same email goes to Harsh (WhatsApp) or its own reply.
Never: Answer the brand's earlier email inside the cut email, promise the revised cut 'for a final check' when this IS the revised cut, or ask a brand that pays through a platform (Gusto) or already got 3 billing reminders for their billing details. When the brand asks US to send billing details, never reply by asking for theirs.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.
## Approved with one change means changes for the editor
When: A brand approves a cut but asks for one change in the same email (music, a caption, a frame)
Do: Put the video's EDIT TRACKER row on Changes with the brand's words in Brand Feedback and the board card on 8- Changes, so the editor fixes it and the revised cut goes straight back to the brand. Anything else in the email (billing details, a date) is handled on its own.
Never: Hold the whole email for Harsh because the readers disagree on approval vs feedback, or treat it as a full approval and post the cut unchanged.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.
## One EDIT TRACKER row per video
When: Adding or creating an EDIT TRACKER row for a video (by hand, from a brief page, or when an edit was delivered without the buttons)
Do: Look up existing rows with the same Video ID first. If one exists, update that row (status, dates, note) instead of adding a new one.

## Let the n8n watcher send the editor's changes alert
When: The PM sets an EDIT TRACKER row to Changes from a brand email
Do: Set Status to Changes and fill Brand Feedback only. Leave Changes Requested At empty: the n8n EDIT TRACKER watcher sends the tagged 'CHANGES REQUESTED' alert within 2 minutes and stamps that field itself. The PM's own thread post is only a fallback after 20 minutes.
Never: Never stamp Changes Requested At from the PM (it makes the watcher think the alert already went out), and never ask Harsh to add settings to fix something that used to work: find what changed.

## Brand changes move the board card to 8
When: A brand sends change notes on a cut that is with them
Do: Set the EDIT TRACKER row to Changes, ping the editor, and move the creator's board card back to 8- Changes at the same moment.
Never: Never leave the board card on 9- Approval while the editor is working on brand changes.

When: A brand approves a cut and names publishing days
Do: The same day, put the card at 10- To Post with a POST DATE inside the brand's window and tell the team. If the date passes with nothing live, tell Harsh once with the brand's latest message. Take the invoice due date from the contract terms (Net 30 = invoice date + 30), not the Stripe default.
Never: Let an approved video sit unposted for days while the brand chases, or record it only as 'Waiting on us' with no card or date.

## Cut with the brand means board card at 9
When: An edited cut goes to the brand, by Send to Brand or by approving a Draft video email
Do: Move the creator's board card to 9- Approval Brand/Creator together with the EDIT TRACKER row going to With Brand, and only move it forward from 6, 7 or 8.
Never: Never leave the board card on 7- In Edit while the video is waiting on the brand.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.
## Editor page shows the approved script
When: An editor opens a video's brief page
Do: Show the approved version from the Script sub-page (the version marked approved/final, else the latest).
Never: Show no script or an old version.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.
## Editors get the brand's full notes
When: Passing brand notes to an editor
Do: Send every line, and the Discord Changes alert must show them under 'What to fix'.
Never: Send only the first line, or an alert without the notes.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: Rulebook.
## Every Raw Footage folder is shared by link
When: A Drive folder is made for a video
Do: Share it with anyone with the link before giving it out.
Never: Hand out a private folder.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.
## A cut can't wait unseen in review
When: A cut is In Review on EDIT TRACKER
Do: Remind once a day, and right away when the go-live date is close.
Never: Let it sit until the post date passes.

## Each video's cut email stands alone
When: Sending or drafting a cut for one video
Do: Only replace an older cut email for the same video (same Frame.io link or title).
Never: Reject another video's revised cut.

## Editor page reads each board's own column names
When: Showing card fields on the editor brief page
Do: Match REF, Ref Video, Edited Vid and similar.

## Brand change notes go to the editor
When: A brand sends notes on a cut or a script
Do: Put the notes on the right video row and send them to the editor (cut) or Rudraksh (script). After the editor is done, draft the revised-cut email.

# LINDSAY — DESIGN FILE (Motion Graphics)

Notion page, last edited 2026-10-02.

This page is the single source of truth for Lindsay's motion graphics. Claude reads it at the start of every Lindsay video, so whatever you change here is used in the next build.
  - To change something: edit it directly, then add a line to the Change log at the bottom (date, your name, what changed).
  - Not sure? Leave a Notion comment on the line instead of editing.
  - Status: v0.3 (draft). Built from Lindsay's own videos, reference videos v01–v08, frames f01–f04 and typography t01–t04.

## 1. What we deliver
- We make motion-graphic clips only. The editor assembles the final video (footage, captions, cuts, sound).
- No captions. Headline typography only: the word or phrase that should hit on screen.
- Every graphic is either:
- For every video we hand over: a preview (full video with graphics), a transparent overlay (HEVC with alpha, so the editor can place Lindsay in split or full screen), EDIT-NOTES with timecodes, and a CLONE.mp3 (only her on-screen lines, silences removed).

## 2. Pacing and retention
- New graphic every ~1.8 s (1.7–2.4 s). Nothing holds longer than ~4 s without something moving inside it.
- Inside a graphic, something changes every 0.5–1 s (a card lands, a number ticks, a cursor clicks).
- Never more than 2 TOP (split) graphics in a row; the next one goes FULL.
- At least 40 % of graphics are FULL. Big reveals (the tool's name, the key screen, lists, the output file) are always FULL.
- Hook: open on Lindsay (TOP) for the first line, then go FULL on the payoff visual. No cuts until the first sentence ends.
- About 60–70 % of lines get a graphic. Lines with nothing concrete to show stay on Lindsay.

## 3. Safe zone (Instagram / TikTok UI)
Important graphics and text go in the white area. The red area only if really needed. Backgrounds and footage may fill the red area; titles, numbers, logos, labels and key UI may not.

## 4. Colours
Sampled from Lindsay's own videos (colour only — don't copy her old edits).
- One background per clip. A tool's own brand colour may replace gold for that tool's moment.

## 5. Typography
- Sans: Inter Display 700–800, tight tracking (−0.03em), sentence case. Headlines and labels.
- Emphasis: Playfair Display Italic, lowercase, for the one word that matters.
  - Regular weight next to the sans: "I built a system" (t04).
  - Black weight in green or coral when it's the word (t01).
  - Keywords in curly quotes: “cloud” (t03).
- Sizes (1080 px canvas): hero word 150–180 px · headline 96–120 px · label 44–56 px.
- One headline per graphic, max 3–4 words, never more than 2 lines.
- Open question: keep these free fonts, or switch to Lindsay's licensed brand fonts?

## 6. Motion
- Signature entry "rise + focus": every element rises from +40 px below while blurred (16 → 0 px), fades in and scales 0.96 → 1 over 0.45 s. Groups stagger 0.08–0.12 s.
- Exits: fast (0.2 s) fade + blur, or a hard cut. Most clips end on a 0.5 s hold.
- Tool name: decodes left to right, letters flicking through 2–3 glyphs (~0.5 s).
- Cross-out: icon greys in → full colour → red line draws corner to corner.
- Numbers always count up. Big money or counts use the flip counter.
- Cursor: real macOS cursor on a slight curve; click = small bounce + ripple.
- Camera: slow push-in on UIs, punch-in on the exact element. No zoom on Claude chat typing frames.
- Never: spins, bouncy text, wipes, glitch transitions, emoji, shaky cam.

## 7. Real assets only
- Logos, app icons and interfaces are always real (screenshots, screen recordings, official launch footage). Never redraw a logo or fake a UI.
- When Lindsay talks about Claude chat, show the real Claude chat UI with the prompt typed in.
- When she shows a tool or extension, use a real screen recording of it. Blur bookmarks bars and anything private.
- App icons: rounded squares (22 % radius), soft shadow. Screenshots: window frame, 16–24 px radius, 1 px border, soft shadow.
- Never invent numbers or claims. If a number in the script can't be sourced, flag it.

## 8. Which graphic for which line
Lindsay's favourites — reach for these first: G16, G17, G18, G19, G20, G15.
Rule of thumb: if she names something, show that exact thing. If she names a number, count it up. If she names several things, each gets its own card on its own word.

- Per video: preview, transparent overlay (HEVC), edit notes with timecodes, CLONE.mp3 of his on-screen lines.

## 3. Base rules (same as all clients)
- New graphic every ~1.8 s; something moves inside a graphic every 0.5–1 s; nothing static longer than ~4 s.
- Never more than 2 split (TOP) graphics in a row. At least 40 % FULL. Big reveals always FULL.
- Hook: strong, with several visual changes, and no cut until the first sentence ends.
- If he names something, show that exact thing. Numbers always count up. Several things in one line → one visual per word.
- Real assets only: real logos, UIs, product visuals and screen recordings. Never fake a UI or redraw a logo. Never invent numbers.

#### Safe zone
Important graphics and text in the white area; red only if really needed. FULL: y 211–1464 (right edge 1025 above y 938, 915 below). TOP: y 211–938, x 55–1025.

## 6. Typography
- Sans: Inter Display 700–800, tight tracking. Two-tone lines: light grey regular + bold on the key word (“First, the model cuts”).
- Emphasis: Playfair Display Italic in red (“A fresh skill”, “QWEN”).
- Ordinals: grey serif italic (“1st”, “2nd”).
- Pixel lettering only inside Minecraft-style moments.

## 7. Motion
- Zooms: slow and premium. 1.2–2 s ease-in-out, max ~15 %, onto the exact thing (the GitHub repo name, the key line). No fast or generic zooms.
- Cursor: realistic mouse moves to the Claude prompt box, clicks, and the prompt types in.
- Emphasis pop-ups for key phrases like “completely free” or “[amount]”.
- Seamless, continuous edit: zoom-through and match transitions; smooth white → black around a logo zoom. It should feel like one intentional sequence, not separate clips.
- Results in, results out: show the output or the models, then clear or transform them as the narration moves on.
- Signature entry (house): rises from below while blurred, then snaps into focus.
- Never: spins, bouncy text, glitch, cheap fast zooms.

## 8. Inspiration — what to copy

### Video 1 — hook, clicks, pop-ups, premium zooms
- Strong hook with multiple visual changes to keep retention high.
- Realistic mouse-click animations when entering prompts in Claude.
- Pop-ups/emphasis graphics for key phrases like “completely free”.
- Slow, premium zooms on important UI/text, especially the GitHub name. Smooth and controlled, never generic or fast.

### Video 2 — seamless transitions, real models, white → black
- Seamless editing and transitions.
- When several AI models are mentioned, show the actual models.
- Show the results/outputs, then remove or transition them as the narration progresses.
- Replicate the smooth white-to-black transition, especially around the Qwen logo zoom.
- Continuous and intentional, not disconnected clips.

### Video 5 — premium, real product visuals
- Premium motion graphics: polished, cinematic, high-end.
- When a product/feature is mentioned (e.g. Claude Opus), show the real product image or visual.

### Video 6 — real screen recordings
- For a GitHub repo and similar, use the real screen recording.
- Show the actual interface so viewers immediately understand it.
- Keep recordings clean (no bookmarks bar, nothing private) and integrated naturally.

## 9. Minecraft / pixel vibe (selective)
- Use a Minecraft-style visual language only where it fits the story: a process with steps, a “build” moment, a playful contrast. About 1–3 moments per video.
- Don't force it everywhere. It should add visual interest or reinforce the point.
- Keep it premium and intentional: pixel icons on his clean grid/white background next to real UIs. Not overly game-like.

- Generic, fast or cheap zooms.
- Disconnected clips with hard cuts where a transition would flow.
- Fake UIs or mocked-up products.
